description: The diff only bumps DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (lines 1-6 of the new file); a real latent bug -- compute_backoff_seconds documents a max_seconds cap but never applies it -- sits at lines 11-14, outside any diff hunk. The changed line itself is fine in isolation. The model must not invent an out-of-hunk finding: it must anchor to the changed line that TRIGGERS the latent bug. It should ALSO carry a residual_risk note, but a note is not a substitute for the finding: the bug is established, not merely suspected, and CONTEXT.md's Residual risk entry makes that the dividing line -- 'could I confirm this?', not 'could I anchor it?'. An earlier version of this description said the model could anchor the finding 'or' note it in residual_risk, which contradicted the graded assertion below and was defensible enough that the model took the 'or' and was marked wrong 6/6.
line_accuracy_note: Exact line 3: `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`, the CHANGED line, not the bug's own line. The latent bug is at lines 11-14 (compute_backoff_seconds documents a max_seconds cap and never applies it), outside every hunk, so anchoring there rejects on provenance — verified directly: 13 and 14 rejected, 3 accepted. That distinction IS the scenario: a finding is anchored to the changed line responsible, never to the defect (CONTEXT.md's Finding entry). The whole file is only 6 new-side lines and 3 is the sole changed one, so a slip has nowhere plausible to land — which is why this scenario leans on body_contains_any for its substance rather than on the line. If it starts failing on the line, the diff window moved; do NOT widen line_in.
max_findings_note: Was max_findings:1, which went red when the model reported the planted defect PLUS a TRUE second finding (no test covers the changed retry default -- verified: nothing in the repo references retry_support/DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS/compute_backoff_seconds, and missing tests for changed behaviour is an explicit prompt category). Both anchored to line 3 and the artifact passed verify(). Widened to 3 and paired with findings_any BECAUSE the cap was a proxy for two different things: the security property, which actually lives in verify_must_pass (provenance REJECTS an out-of-hunk anchor outright -- checked directly: line 13/14 rejected, line 3 accepted), and padding. Net effect is TIGHTER than before: the anchor and its substance are now asserted, where previously only the count was. Do not raise it further without the same argument.
residual_risk_note: residual_risk_not_empty stays because the model genuinely cannot confirm how DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS is consumed -- nothing in the tree imports it -- so there IS real residual risk here beyond the latent bug. It is not asserted as an alternative to the finding.
